summary: Port reproduces the spider's geometry, crawl path, speed and cadence, but draws its eight legs as 1-px hairlines instead of thick tapered wedges and truncates the leg palette before green, so on the pattern's own 16x16 rig it reads as a red dot surrounded by scattered specks rather than a spider.
observations: Both sides render without compile or runtime errors; neither exposes any settable control (probe: 'no settable controls' on orig and port), and neither binds sensors (wantsSensors false both sides).

Shared concept confirmed at 48x48 (label grid48): both draw a red/orange body blob with EIGHT legs radiating outward that wiggle frame-to-frame, and both walk the figure diagonally across the grid and off an edge, then re-enter.

Leg weight is the headline structural difference. At 48x48 the original's legs are thick tapered wedges (lit area 18.8%/27.2%/15.6% of the grid at t=3.15/4.4/5.75 s); the port's are single-pixel dashed lines (5.5%/9.8%/8.5%) — roughly a third of the original's lit area at every sampled moment.

On the DEFAULT 16x16 rig that hairline width aliases the port's spider apart. Eight-connected component analysis of dumped frames (label dump-geom, t=3.15-7.0 s): original = 1 connected blob of 40-63 lit pixels with 0 isolated pixels in 5 of 7 frames; port = 5-10 separate components, 3-9 of them single isolated pixels, largest component only 6-19 px. The port's legs never touch its body at native resolution.
Lit-pixel count at 16x16 peak (label dump-track, centroid sampling once per second over 60 s): original peaks at 63-70 lit pixels per crawl, port at 21-30 — ~2.8x fewer.

Palette is truncated on the port. Original leg tips reach saturated green (e.g. RGB 0,255,19 and 30,255,0 in the t=4 dump): over 45 lit frames of dump-track, 32 contained at least one green pixel and green was 16.7% of all lit pixels. Port over 37 lit frames: 1 frame with any green, 0.2% of lit pixels. Port's ramp stops at red -> orange -> yellow (olive at dimmest, e.g. 93,93,0), never green. Blue channel is 0 on both sides throughout.

Overall brightness: original meanBrightness avg 12.3 (baseline) / 9.8 (survey) / 9.6 (survey-240); port 3.3 / 2.5 / 2.3 — about 4x dimmer, which is the ~2.8x lit-area deficit multiplied by dimmer lit pixels (mean lit value 190-198 orig vs 132-146 port at t=3 and t=4).

Spider size: peak radial extent from the weighted centroid at 16x16 is 5.6-7.6 px on the original vs 4.1-5.6 px on the port; at 48x48 it is 19.6-24.6 vs 15.5-21.2 — the port's figure is consistently ~0.8x the original's reach.

Motion matches well. Horizontal crawl speed measured from weighted centroids is ~2.7 px/s (orig, x 13.3 -> 0.0 over t=2-7 s) vs ~2.8 px/s (port, x 0.0 -> 13.9 over the same window) on the 16x16 rig; both also drift vertically, so the walk is diagonal on both sides.

Both sides randomize crawl direction per traverse — over 60 s the original ran R->L, R->L, L->R, L->R, L->R, R->L, L->R and the port L->R, R->L, R->L, L->R, L->R, L->R — so the differing direction in any single window is RNG, not a port bug.

Cycle timing differs slightly. Autocorrelation of meanBrightness (survey, 300 frames @5 fps) peaks at 45 frames = 9.0 s for the original and 100 frames = 20.0 s (with a 50-frame = 10.0 s harmonic) for the port; the 240 s survey agrees (orig lags 18/36/54 s off a 9 s base, port 20/40/60 s off a 10 s base). Crawl-start times over 60 s: orig 2,10,20,28,37,46,55 s (intervals 8-10 s, variable); port 2,12,22,32,42,52 s (interval exactly 10 s).

The extra second per cycle sits in the dark gap between crawls: the original goes fully dark for ~2.5-3 s between traverses, the port for ~4-4.5 s (regime-gap, --skip 6.5: orig's gap runs ~7.3-10.6 s, port's ~7.2-11.7 s). Some of this is likely secondary to the port's smaller, dimmer figure vanishing earlier and appearing later at the grid edge.

Both sides are resolution-independent in the same way: lit fraction stays roughly constant across 8x8, 16x16 and 48x48 (orig ~17-27%, port ~5.5-10% at all three), so the port matches the original's mapping onto the rig — it is only the leg weight that is wrong, not the scaling rule.

Both sides are fps-invariant (time-based, not frame-stepped): centroid x at t=1..19 s is essentially identical at --fps 10 and --fps 40 on both sides (e.g. orig 13.3/12.0/8.9/4.6 vs 13.8/12.2/9.2/4.9; port 0.0/1.6/4.3/8.3 vs 0.0/1.7/4.4/8.2). No frame-rate coupling divergence.
Findings hold at seeds 7 and 1234 as well as the default seed 1: the original still shows a full green-tipped spider, the port still shows a red body with detached yellow/orange specks.
zeroMotionFrames is high on both (baseline: 33/120 orig, 41/120 port), i.e. both re-pose the legs at a sub-frame-rate cadence — not a divergence.
feedback: Thicken the legs. The original draws each of the eight legs as a tapered wedge several pixels wide near the body narrowing toward the tip; the port draws a 1-px line. Target the original's lit area: at 48x48 the original lights 16-27% of the grid at peak versus the port's 5.5-10%, and on the default 16x16 rig 40-70 lit pixels versus the port's 21-30. Right now the port's legs are so thin they break into isolated single pixels on the 16x16 rig (5-10 disconnected components per frame versus the original's single blob) — the fix must keep the legs contiguous with the body at 16x16, which is the pattern's own rig.

Extend the leg color ramp into green. The original's gradient runs red body -> orange -> yellow -> saturated green at the tips (pure values like 0,255,19 appear); the port stops at yellow and never emits green (green in 1 of 37 lit frames versus 32 of 45 for the original). Push the far end of the per-leg gradient past yellow into green rather than clamping there.

Raise overall output ~4x. The original averages meanBrightness ~10-12 over 60-240 s windows; the port averages ~2.3-3.3. Most of that comes back with the thicker legs, but the port's lit pixels are also individually dimmer (mean lit value ~135-145 versus the original's ~190-198), so the body/leg intensity envelope needs lifting too.
Grow the figure ~25%. The port's spider reaches only ~0.8x the original's radius (16x16 peak extent 4.1-5.6 px versus 5.6-7.6 px; 48x48 15.5-21.2 versus 19.6-24.6).

Shorten the pause between traverses and let it vary. The original's crawl cycle is ~9 s and irregular (traverse starts at 2,10,20,28,37,46,55 s), with ~2.5-3 s fully dark between crawls; the port's is a rigid 10 s (starts at 2,12,22,32,42,52 s) with a ~4-4.5 s dark gap. The crawl speed itself is already right (~2.7 px/s on both), so the correction belongs in the inter-crawl dwell, not the walking speed.

Do not change: crawl speed, diagonal walk, the eight-leg count and radial arrangement, the per-frame leg wiggle, the random per-traverse direction, resolution independence, and fps invariance all already match the original.
